entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mīrzā Muhammad Tarāghāy bin Shāhrukh, better known as Ulugh Beg, was a Timurid sultan, as well as an astronomer and mathematician.

    Born into the royal family of the Timurid Empire in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, around 1394, Ulugh Beg's early life was marked by the struggle for power in the post-Timurid era. He eventually seized the throne in 1409 and ruled until his death in 1449. Ulugh Beg's reign was characterized by significant cultural, scientific, and economic achievements.

    One of his most notable accomplishments was the compilation of the Ulugh Beg Observatory in Samarkand, which became a major center of astronomical learning and innovation in the 15th century. He also made significant contributions to mathematics, particularly in the field of trigonometry, and wrote several influential works on the subject.

    Ulugh Beg's legacy extended beyond his scientific contributions, as he also played a crucial role in the development of the Timurid Empire's diplomatic and trade relations with neighboring regions. He maintained a network of ambassadors and merchants who traveled extensively throughout the Middle East, Europe, and Asia, exchanging goods, ideas, and cultures.

    Despite his many achievements, Ulugh Beg's reign was also marked by conflict and power struggles with neighboring rulers and the rise of the Ottoman Empire. His death in 1449 marked the beginning of a new era of instability in the region, but his legacy as a patron of learning and a unifying force for the Timurid Empire endured.
